text: The Swami Vivekananda Planetarium, also known as Pilikula Planetarium, is located at Pilikula Nisargadhama in Mangaluru and is the first 3D planetarium in India. It is the only such planetarium in the country equipped with hybrid modern technology, combining 8K digital and opto-mechanical (hybrid) projection systems. Part of the Pilikula Nisargadhama, which spans 370 acres (150 ha) and is named Dr. Shivaram Karanth Biological Park, the planetarium was initiated in 2013 to commemorate the 150th birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda by then Karnataka Chief Minister Jagadish Shettar. The foundation stone was laid by Shettar, and the project was undertaken at a cost of ₹35.69 crore (US$4.2 million), with the construction completed two years later than planned, opening on 1 March 2018. The planetarium was established with grants from KSTePS (Karnataka Science and Technology Promotion Society). It is operated by the Pilikula Regional Science Centre and aims to provide viewers—especially students and the public—with immersive experiences of stars and planetary systems. The planetarium features an 18 m (59 ft) diameter dome with a seating capacity of 170, where seats can be tilted by 15 degrees to improve viewing. It uses a Megastar IIA optical projector integrated with a Digistar and active stereo 3D 8K digital system manufactured by Evans & Sutherland Computer Corporation in the US, along with 32 lenses from Ohira Tech Japan, capable of projecting "20 million stars uniformly and seamlessly" across the dome’s nano-seam panels without visual overlap. Five technical personnel were initially trained in Utah, US, to operate the facility, and the planetarium includes a ₹1.5 crore (US$180,000) annual maintenance fund. It inaugurated on 1 March 2018 and began its first public show on 2 March 2018, offering eight shows daily, each lasting 25 minutes. The shows, such as We are stars, Dawn of the space age, and Mysteries of the unseen world, cover space technology, planets, nature, environment science, history, and geography in English, Hindi, and Kannada. The inaugural show, We are stars, narrates the story of space from the Big Bang to the present day. The planetarium is situated at Moodushedde, 9 kilometres (5.6 mi) from Mangalore, well connected by road, rail, and air. Mangalore Railway Station links to major cities like Chennai, Mumbai, and New Delhi, while Mangalore International Airport is about 7 kilometres (4.3 mi) from the city centre. By road, it is 350 kilometres (220 mi) west of Bengaluru, the capital of Karnataka.
